1.explanation:
• docs/bug-repros/issue-1340/index.qmd: a known bug‐repro page that shows how code‐chunk options (including echo) are handled in a minimal `.qmd` example.  
• docs/languages/mermaid/test1-jupyter.qmd and test1-rmd.qmd: the official Mermaid integration tests in Quarto for Jupyter and R Markdown—these illustrate how Mermaid chunks are parsed and rendered, and are the basis for spotting differences when echo is enabled.  
• docs/test-knitr-options.qmd: demonstrates how Quarto translates typical knitr chunk options (including echo and fenced echo) into rendered output, which is directly related to why an extra blank line might be injected.  
• docs/test-singleformat-html.qmd: shows how a single‐format HTML document renders code chunks by default, useful for comparing the phantom line insertion when `echo: true` is toggled.  
• docs/test-plain.md: a plain‐text markdown test that shows baseline code‐block rendering without Quarto enhancements—useful to confirm that the blank line is introduced by Quarto’s chunk‐processing rather than the browser or CSS.
1.bug_scenario: The user has a Quarto `.qmd` document containing Mermaid (and similarly dot) code chunks with the chunk option `echo: true` (or `echo: fenced`). When rendered to HTML, the output code block shows an unwanted blank line at the very top of the chunk. The screenshots show on the left the source chunk (with `%%| echo: true` or `%%| echo: fenced`) and on the right the rendered code block, where the first line is empty, pushing all of the diagram code down by one line. This occurs for both Mermaid and Graphviz (`dot`) chunks.
